original_question: Suppose λ is singular and 2^λ > λ^+. Does ZFC prove that for every α < λ^+, every 2-coloring of λ^+ × λ has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A| = α and |B| = λ, i.e. \((λ^+ over λ) → (α over λ)^(1,1)_2\) for all α < λ^+?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.8: whether, for a singular cardinal λ with 2^λ > λ^+, one has \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\alpha}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2 for every \alpha < \lambda^+.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the paper’s actual target: λ is singular, the hypothesis is 2^λ > λ^+, the question quantifies over every α < λ^+, it is about 2-colorings of λ^+ × λ, and the desired conclusion is the polarized relation \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\alpha}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2.
missing_details: In the paper this is posed as an open problem (Problem 4.8), not as a theorem proved there.
The hypothesis is stated exactly as λ > cf(λ) and 2^λ > λ^+; Problem 4.8 itself does not assume that λ is strong limit.

The parameter α is an ordinal below λ^+; in the partition-calculus notation used here, the first monochromatic set should have order type α, so replacing this by |A| = α is not fully faithful unless α is a cardinal.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should explicitly say that for every coloring c: λ^+ × λ → 2 there are A ⊆ λ^+ and B ⊆ λ such that c is constant on A × B.

The nearby context matters: Problem 4.8 is explicitly presented as a strengthening of the recalled result that if λ is strong limit singular and 2^λ > λ^+, then \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\lambda+1}{\lambda}^{1,1}_\theta for every \theta < cf(λ).

A second nearby benchmark is Theorem 2.7: if λ is a limit of measurable cardinals, then the stronger conclusion \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\alpha}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2 for every α < λ^+ is already known in ZFC.
refined_question: Assume that λ is a singular cardinal with λ > cf(λ) and 2^λ > λ^+. Is it a theorem of ZFC that for every ordinal α < λ^+ and every coloring c: λ^+ × λ → 2, there exist sets A ⊆ λ^+ and B ⊆ λ of order types α and λ, respectively, such that c is constant on A × B; equivalently in the paper’s notation, does \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\alpha}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2 hold for every α < λ^+?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 4, Problem 4.8 almost verbatim. Right before that problem, the paper recalls a weaker theorem from [S3]: if λ is strong limit singular and 2^λ > λ^+, then one already gets \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\lambda+1}{\lambda}^{1,1}_\theta for every \theta < cf(λ). Problem 4.8 then asks for exactly the strengthening your draft is trying to express, namely whether one can replace that weaker conclusion by \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\alpha}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2 for every α < λ^+ under only singularity of λ and 2^λ > λ^+. Theorem 2.7 gives the nearby comparison case where this stronger conclusion is already known in ZFC when λ is a limit of measurable cardinals. Definition 1.1 supplies the paper’s monochromatic-rectangle reading of polarized notation in the strong case, and Corollary 5.3 shows that the paper later proves consistency of an even stronger full relation by forcing, rather than resolving Problem 4.8 in ZFC.
